claims.statement: The .t3kpreset on-disk format (plugin/include/PresetFile.h, shared by PresetManager and tools/preset_tool.cpp — depends only on juce_core + juce_data_structures so the latter needs neither the processor nor NAM) has two framings read, one written: v2 = "T3KH" | int32 LE headerBytes | header ValueTree | body ValueTree; v1 (legacy) = "T3KB" | body ValueTree. The header is a tiny ValueTree ("T3KPresetHeader": id, name) so listing a preset folder reads a few hundred bytes per file instead of deserializing the megabytes of model bytes each body embeds; the body repeats id and name so a reader that only knows the body still has everything. Legacy files fall back to a full parse for their header fields; PresetManager rewrites them as v2 on their next save/rename. PresetFile::write() writes then renames, so a failure never clobbers the target.

UiPrefs gained the t3k.nodeView key (UiPrefs::kNodeView, UiPrefs.h:68) for the gallery|node view toggle in the 2026-10-17 node-view ticket. It is stored as a plain string round-tripped by UiPrefs::getBool (UiPrefs.cpp:33-37: "true" → true, "false" → false, anything else → the fallback), with PluginHeader seeding the toggle from prefs.getBool(UiPrefs::kNodeView, false) and the testbed seeding it via the fixture's "localStorage" block. Like all UiPrefs keys it lives in the shared prefs file, NOT in .t3kpreset bodies.

The DAW-host state blob (getStateInformation/setStateInformation, plugin/src/ProcessorState.cpp:640-712) is `T3KB` magic (kStateMagic, :35) + one format-flag byte + payload: flag 1 = gzip (8-byte LITTLE-ENDIAN original size + a zlib-wrapped stream from juce::GZIPCompressorOutputStream at level -1), flag 0 = raw binary ValueTree bytes; a 5th byte that is neither flag is a legacy no-flag save parsed from offset 4 (kStateSchemaVersion is 2, :45; the tree itself carries schemaVersion, bumped 1→2 by the optimization-findings Stage 1 commit 353bac9, and setStateInformation at :717 rejects blobs whose embedded version exceeds kStateSchemaVersion). The gzip layer is chosen only when it is strictly smaller — incompressible payloads (the LCG test rig) save flag 0; real 360 KB-class NAM captures save flag 1 (StateSize* tests in test/src/state_size_tests.cpp pin both). The payload is binary, not the original Base64-in-XML: that path burned 100+ ms per host save on a heavy rig. This is the DAW-host state path ONLY — the T3KB/T3KH preset FILE format (PresetManager 3-tier + factory presets) is a separate compat surface and is untouched by these stages.
